results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response:
There are multiple types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain, including alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells. These can be further subdivided into core/surface/posterior, anterior-posterior/middle, dorsal/main/gamma-s/gamma-t, and claw-count classes. VFB's ontology places 7 direct subtypes under [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), 22 subtypes in all across 2 levels. VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of Kenyon cell.

results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response:
The [adult central brain](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047887 "Open adult central brain in Virtual Fly Brain") contains approximately 32,388 neurons, according to FlyWire. VFB has annotated [9,413](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047887,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult central brain") neuron types with some part in the adult central brain.

**Published neuron-count estimates — adult central brain** (from the literature):

- ~32,388 neurons (Whole adult brain, both optic lobes and ocellar ganglia included. Ventral nerve cord NOT included; neurons crossing the neck connective are truncated at the brain boundary. Subcount: fully in central brain. One female adult. Dataset: FlyWire connectome neurons, v783.) — [Dorkenwald S et al. (2024) Nature 634(8032):124-138 — PMID 39358518](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07558-y "Open Dorkenwald S et al. (2024) Nature 634(8032):124-138 — PMID 39358518 via DOI (new tab)")

_FlyWire reports 32,388 neurons FULLY CONTAINED in the central brain out of 139,255 in the whole brain. Neurons that arborise in the central brain but also elsewhere are not in that subcount, so it is a lower bound on 'neurons in the central brain', not a census of them._

_VFB has annotated 9,413 neuron types with some part in adult central brain — a curated annotation count, not the biological total._

Reference: [How many neurons are in the fly brain?](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/docs/concepts/neuron-counts/ "Open “How many neurons are in the fly brain?” — Virtual Fly Brain documentation (new tab)")

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response: The main components of the Drosophila central complex include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the three paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge. These components are associated with functions such as navigation and orientation, locomotor control, and sleep/arousal and memory-related behaviours. The answer uses the reading of "[adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003632 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain")" as the central complex itself, but VFB also holds data under this name for related structures including the anterior chiasma of the central complex, posterior chiasma of the central complex, central complex neuroblast, and [adult central complex on adult brain template JFRC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_00030866 "Open adult central complex on adult brain template JFRC2 in Virtual Fly Brain"). VFB holds [363](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003632,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult central complex") records of neurons with some part in the adult central complex and [362](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003632,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in adult central complex") records of neurons with synaptic terminals in the adult central complex.

results.response: The [lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111763 "Open lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") is a type of neuron with a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer. This arrangement allows it to detect looming (expansion) stimuli and its activity elicits a jump escape response. In the lobula, it has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. Its arbors span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells. The LPLC2 projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. There are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe and they are cholinergic.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior. It has a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum and a large descending axon that enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle. In the brain, it has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget. The giant fiber neuron forms electrical synapses with downstream motor and premotor neurons at the inframedial bridge and at the axonal lateral bend.

The giant fiber neuron connects to several downstream neuron classes, including [mesothoracic extracoxal trochanter depressor muscle motor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053153 "Open mesothoracic extracoxal trochanter depressor muscle motor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult efferent neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051964 "Open adult efferent neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [NB3-3 lineage primary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00048874 "Open NB3-3 lineage primary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult IN18B034 neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20010307 "Open adult IN18B034 neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [peripherally synapsing interneuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007408 "Open peripherally synapsing interneuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult premotor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051437 "Open adult premotor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage primary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047106 "Open Notch ON hemilineage primary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [adult IN06B008 neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20009235 "Open adult IN06B008 neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). It also connects to itself.

There are available driver lines for the giant fiber neuron, including [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") split-GAL4 combinations. Regarding the connection between the visual system and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain"), VFB's "Neurons with some part in mushroom body" query and "Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body" query return results that include various neuron types, such as larval uniglomerular projection neurons and larval antennal lobe multiglomerular projection neurons. The documentation also describes the circuit diagram of the mushroom body, which includes MBON cell-types that send axons into the MB lobes.

It is plausible that there is a multi-step pathway between the visual system and the mushroom body, given that adult visual projection neurons have presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body.

results.title: Novel circuit exploration
results.question: What is the connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body? Could temperature information influence memory formation?
results.response:
The connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") is supported by VFB evidence, which suggests a plausible thermosensory influence on mushroom-body memory circuitry through thermosensory projection neurons. This influence is indicated by downstream evidence to mushroom body dopaminergic neurons and Kenyon cell classes.

VFB's class-level connectivity table for [thermosensory neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005918 "Open thermosensory neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") lists [2,400](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005918,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for thermosensory neuron") downstream classes and [1,538](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005918,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for thermosensory neuron") upstream classes. The strongest specific targets of thermosensory neuron include [adult antennal lobe projection neuron VP2 adPN](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00048093 "Open adult antennal lobe projection neuron VP2 adPN in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult antennal lobe projection neuron VP2 l2PN](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049730 "Open adult antennal lobe projection neuron VP2 l2PN in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [adult antennal lobe local neuron l2LN21](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20003737 "Open adult antennal lobe local neuron l2LN21 in Virtual Fly Brain"), among others. The strongest specific inputs to thermosensory neuron include [adult antennal lobe local neuron l2LN22](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20003738 "Open adult antennal lobe local neuron l2LN22 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult oligoglomerular local interneuron of the lateral AL neuroblast](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007404 "Open adult oligoglomerular local interneuron of the lateral AL neuroblast in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [antennal lobe local neuron 4](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047708 "Open antennal lobe local neuron 4 in Virtual Fly Brain").

VFB also provides information on neurons with synaptic terminals in the mushroom body, with [601](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body") results. The first 12 results include [adult odd neuron of the calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111628 "Open adult odd neuron of the calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), [larval uniglomerular projection neuron 63a](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111675 "Open larval uniglomerular projection neuron 63a in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [larval uniglomerular projection neuron 67b](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111684 "Open larval uniglomerular projection neuron 67b in Virtual Fly Brain"), among others. Additionally, VFB lists [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body and [304](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPostsynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with postsynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with postsynaptic terminals in the mushroom body.

Temperature information could potentially influence memory formation through the connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body. However, the exact nature of this influence is not fully detailed in VFB evidence.

results.question: I'm interested in studying the subesophageal zone (SEZ). How well-characterised is this region in VFB? What neuron types are annotated, what connectomics data is available, and what genetic tools exist for SEZ neurons?

VFB returned 4205 genetic tool/expression pattern rows for subesophageal zone, indicating the existence of genetic tools such as GAL4 drivers and binary/intersectional drivers for SEZ neurons. Connectomics data available for the SEZ includes downstream and upstream connectivity classes, as well as transgene expression reports and split-GAL4 combinations. Downstream connectivity classes for the larval subesophageal zone descending SEZ DN neuron are available, and can be queried for their count. Transgene expression in the larval subesophageal zone descending SEZ DN neuron is also available, and can be queried for the count.

results.response: NBLAST is a method for calculating similarity scores between neurons or expression patterns. VFB provides precomputed NBLAST scores to assist in the discovery of morphologically similar neurons and potential split-GAL4 driver lines.

turns.question: What is the fan-shaped body?
turns.response: The [fan-shaped body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003679 "Open fan-shaped body in Virtual Fly Brain") is the largest synaptic neuropil domain of the adult central complex, located posterior to the ellipsoid body and anterior to the protocerebral bridge. An additional, much narrower, 9th layer, which lacks a columnar organization, sits dorsal to layer 8. The number of columns varies for different neuronal types.

turns.response: The [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") is a bilaterally paired neuropil structure situated postero-dorsally in the protocerebrum that functions in olfactory associative learning and memory. turns.response: The [protocerebral bridge](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003668 "Open protocerebral bridge in Virtual Fly Brain") is a handle bar-shaped synaptic neuropil located just posterior to the fan-shaped body. Its lateral edge ends at the posterior end of the inferior clamp near the medial equatorial fascicle. It forms a dorso-posteriorly located part of the central complex embedded in the cortex between the calyces of the two mushroom bodies, and is composed of a row of 18 connected slices, 9 on each side of the midline, numbered 1-9 from medial to lateral.
